newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Egypt, Malaysia plan four joint projects.
newsitem.headline: Egypt, Malaysia plan four joint projects.

text.p: Egypt and Malaysia have agreed on four joint projects in Egypt involving agriculture, shipyard upgrading, high-technology and oil refining, Egyptian Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri said on Tuesday.

Ganzouri, on a three-day visit to Malaysia, did not disclose the amount of investment for the four projects or name the parties involved. He told a news conference that the agricultural project would involve growing cotton and include textiles production for export.
Discussing the oil refinery project, Ganzouri said: "Egypt right now imports a lot of oil... This will help us to cut imports and also have a chance to export some of that."
On Monday, Malaysia and Egypt signed three trade agreements and two memoranda of understanding on tourism.

The trade agreements, covering the promotion of investment, avoidance of double taxation and prevention of fiscal evasion on income taxes, marked an expansion of the two countries' ties beyond politics and culture.
In 1996, Malaysia's trade with Egypt amounted to 625 million ringgit ($249 million), representing 0.2 per cent of Malaysia's total trade.
Exports from Malaysia to Egypt for the same year amounted to 606 million ringgit while imports totalled 19 million ringgit.
Ganzouri said the Malaysian pacts were part of his country's strategy to invite "friendly countries" to invest in Egypt.

He said after struggling for the last 15 years with unrest in the Middle East, "Egypt has succeeded in establishing a very strong infrastructure", and within the last five years had put in financial and military reforms that have resulted in growth and stability.
He said Egypt had liberalised rules governing foreign investment to ensure the process was "easy" and "secure".
He said Egypt was visiting "friendly countries" beginning with Malaysia to promote foreign investment.
